An Indian information technology company founded in Pune in 1981 by seven engineers, among them N. R. Narayana Murthy and Nandan Nilekani, with a small loan from Murthy's wife. It moved its base to Bengaluru in 1983.

Infosys sold software and IT services to foreign, mostly American, companies, using Indian engineers who cost far less. Early on, red tape made this slow: importing a computer could take years. The economic liberalisation of 1991 freed it up. Its "global delivery model", doing work in India for clients abroad, became the template for the whole industry. In 1999 it became the first Indian company listed on an American stock exchange.

The work needed to fix old software for the year 2000 and the internet boom made it grow fast. It was known for giving shares to staff, which made many employees rich, and for its huge training campus in Mysore. With Tata Consultancy Services, Wipro and others, it made Bengaluru the centre of India's software export boom and created a new middle class of engineers, many from colleges like the IITs. Nilekani later led India's Aadhaar identity scheme, a base for the Unified Payments Interface.
